text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- In the next five years, sales tax is expected to show an annual growth of more than 22 percent, income tax about 22 percent, other direct taxes 17.6 percent while import duties are likely to grow at a relative low rate of 13.7 percent and excise duties at a rate of 15.2 percent.
- Sindh province authorities have arrested former provincial excise and taxation minister Munawwar Talpur and former irrigation minister Zafar Leghari.
- Abdul Qadeer, a former governor of the eastern Afghan province of Nangarhar, will leave Peshawar on Monday under expulsion orders from the Pakistani government for his anti-Taleban activities.
THE NEWS

- An intelligence report presented to the government claims that some 300 tranied terrorists have entered Pakistan to carry out subversive activities in the country during the Moslem mourning month of Muharram.

- Pakistan on Sunday turned down a request of the United States to release Ayaz Baloch, a Pakistani employee of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency arrested for alleged involvement in anti-state activities.

- Scores of prisoners injured in a riot at Adiala Jail near Islamabad on Sunday have refused to take medical treatment. - Mahbubul Haq, a former finance minister and a leading economist, is likely to be inducted in the government of Pakistan Muslim League provided he accepts the status and authority given to him.
THE NATION

- A three-member International Monetary Fund mission will arrive in Islamabad on Monday to hold talks for more than $2 billion Structural Adjustment Facility to be finalised after the budget for fiscal 1996/97.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government is preparing to launch an aggressive population welfare programme.
THE MUSLIM
- Pakistan has been asked by donors to plug leakages in its tax collection system to qualify for financial assistance of $2.68 billion from aid-to-Pakistan consortium.
- Pakistan on Sunday slammed the arrest of prominent Kashmiri leader Shabir Ahmed Shah in the Indian-held Kashmir.

- Pakistan Supreme Court chief justice Sajjad Ali Shah will chair a meeting of the Law Commission on Thursday to review prison laws and a century-old jail manual still followed in the country's prisons.

- The Federal Investigation Agency, which is probing into allegations against the former managing director of Pakistan Television, Raana Shiekh, has found fresh evidence of large-scale financial corruption agaisnt her.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Sunday rang Iranian President Hashemi Rafsanjani to express condolences over the death of 2,400 people killed in earthquake in Iran.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The government, facing a severe resource crunch, has prepared a consolidated action plan to raise $2.58 billion from international market by December 1997 to meet its foreign debt obligations while a $95 million loan due for repayment in July 1997 has been rolled over.
- The government has decided to call a businessmen's convention in a few weeks to take commitments on tax payments.
- Gorwths of earnings of 100 companies of Karachi Stock Exchange will be pushed up by four to six percent over the current estimates of 22 percent for fiscal 1997-98 (July-June).
FINANCIAL POST

- The mini-budget announced by the government was a perfect example of accepting the pre-qualifications of the International Monetary Fund for advancing $1.5 billion under a extended structural adjustment facility programme is due in September, say economists.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
